answers:
Where do my notes live?
+

In this product concept, your notes are stored locally on your device. Lattice is designed around keeping your research close to you, with optional full-text search that also runs locally. This demonstration page does not store notes.

Can I take my notes somewhere else?
+

Yes. Lattice’s proposed Markdown export gives you readable files you can open in a text editor or bring into another Markdown-compatible tool. Your thinking can move with you.

How would I back up my work?
+

Export your notes as files and keep a copy in a separate location you control, such as an external drive. Make exporting a regular habit. Automatic cloud backup is not included or promised.

What happens if I cancel?
+

Cancellation has no effect on files you have already exported. Those files remain yours to read, edit, and keep. The prices and plans here are illustrative; this demo has no active subscriptions to cancel.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The large three-line serif headline is balanced against a mostly upright notebook window. A single dark primary button follows the explanatory paragraph; the bordered header action is secondary.
observations.implication: The desktop page has a clear reading order from proposition to explanation to action, with the notebook illustration serving as a concrete companion.

observations.observation: Large serif headings and green italic phrases recur with a consistent sans-serif body. Explanatory copy in the feature, workflow and FAQ captures is comfortably prominent. Small letter-spaced labels and notebook interface microcopy are much finer than the main text.
observations.implication: The explanatory text is easy to pick out, while the decorative metadata and scaled notebook details are less immediately readable.

observations.observation: Off-white paper surfaces, dark green ink, light sage blocks, thin rules and grid/arrow motifs remain consistent. The workflow uses the same palette inverted into a dark band.
observations.implication: The sections maintain a recognizable editorial notebook identity, rather than a collection of unrelated component styles.

observations.observation: The hero notebook contains a sidebar, note text, a source attachment and tags, with a question card extending outside the frame. The Connect state shows a compact tree connecting one question to field observations and reading notes.
observations.implication: The product model is concrete and the Connect diagram is simple to parse. The capture alone does not establish that the illustrated notebook interface is interactive.

observations.observation: The mobile headline and body are large and fit the captured canvas. The header uses an icon-only menu button. Generous vertical spacing and the longer explanation place the notebook illustration near the bottom edge of the first viewport.
observations.implication: The opening favors readable text and breathing room, but visitors see little of the product illustration before scrolling. The menu is less explicitly labelled visually than a control that includes the word Menu; this is not a claim about its accessible name.

observations.observation: The yearly selector has a distinct dark selected state; the prices, per-year labels and plan contents are plainly separated. The expanded FAQ answer uses a generous line height and column width, with the remaining questions laid out as individual rows.
observations.implication: The captured information states are legible and consistently arranged. No obvious broken layout or clipped primary text is visible in the inspected viewports.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
These static viewport captures do not evaluate motion quality, keyboard behavior, all scroll positions, every responsive breakpoint, or color contrast ratios.
Some anchored desktop captures start partway through a preceding heading; that is viewport framing, not evidence that the source page clips that heading.
The notebook mockups illustrate a fictional product. Their apparent controls are not evidence of implemented notebook functionality.
Both inspected candidates use a coherent serif-and-green editorial direction. These observations do not establish a general winner, causal improvement, or which condition produced either artifact.

processReview.summary: The Fabius landing run read its design reference and used an observed fallback failure to drive a source fix and successful browser retests.

observations.observed: The public outline named design, responsive layouts, keyboard interactions, billing and no-JavaScript checks before the implementation command.
An actual tool command read the pinned design-system reference before implementation.
A browser run failed in the no-JavaScript pricing fallback. The run inspected the failing check and DOM, replaced the fallback with ordinary HTML, and reran the expanded browser suite successfully.
Further commands exercised nested paths, more widths, keyboard states and contrast; another browser run followed the later diagram CSS change. Scripts, captures and limitations were retained.

limits: The initial implementation required a functional fallback correction.
The candidate’s browser checks use Chrome; independent WebKit grading is a separate stage.
The trace shows reference access and a repair loop, not proof that the reference caused the repair.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
